verses.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子约押，知道王心里想念押沙龙，
verses.en: Now Joab son of Zeruiah realized that the king longed to see[NOTE:1] Absalom.
notes: Heb “the heart of the king was upon.” The Syriac Peshitta adds the verb ʾethreʿi (“was reconciled”).
verses.commentary:
14:1 Obviously chapter 14 should not be separated from the flow of 2 Samuel (esp. 13:39). Remember,
capitalization, punctuation, verse divisions, chapter divisions are all recent suggestions but are not inspired.

▣

NASB, NJB
"inclined"

NKJV
"concerned"

NRSV, JPSOA, LXX
"was on"

TEV
"missed. . .very much"

REB
"longed for"

Peshitta
"reconciled"

As you can see from these translation options, there are different ways to view this
PREPOSITION (BDB 752-759). From the context it is uncertain.

- 2 Sam. 13:39 supports a positive sense

- 2 Sam. 14:24 supports a negative sense

- possibly David was simply thinking a lot about Absalom because he was the heir apparent to the throne

verses.zh: 就打发人往提哥亚去，从那里叫了一个聪明的妇人来，对她说：「请你假装居丧的，穿上孝衣，不要用膏抹身，要装作为死者许久悲哀的妇人；
verses.en: So Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman. He told her, “Pretend to be in mourning[NOTE:1] and put on garments for mourning. Don’t anoint yourself with oil. Instead, act like a woman who has been mourning for the dead for some time.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew Hitpael verbal form here indicates pretended rather than genuine action.
Heb “these many days.”
verses.commentary:
14:2-20 This involves a royal judgment, like Nathan's, based on a parable type fictitious story which
described David and Absalom's relationship.

14:2 "a wise woman" This same ADJECTIVE (BDB 314) was used of Jonadab in 2 Sam. 13:3
and another woman in 2 Sam. 20:16. The fact that the same word is used to describe the false wisdom of Sisera's mother
in Jdgs. 5:28-29 shows the latitude of the term. Though women had a second class position in the ANE, their wisdom was
honored.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

▣ "Tekoa" This city is about ten miles south of Jerusalem. It was the hometown of Amos.

▣ "a mourner" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES.

verses.zh: 进去见王，对王如此如此说。」于是约押将当说的话教导了妇人。
verses.en: Go to the king and speak to him in the following fashion.” Then Joab told her what to say.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “put the words in her mouth” (so NASB, NIV).
verses.commentary:
14:3 The king was the ultimate judge in Israel (cf. 2 Sam. 14:5,17,21). This tradition probably went back to
Moses as judge.

▣ "So Joab put the words in her mouth" Joab is the originator of this fictitious parable (cf. v. 19) to
convince David to bring Absalom home to Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 提哥亚妇人到王面前，伏地叩拜，说：「王啊，求你拯救！」
verses.en: So the Tekoan woman went[NOTE:1] to the king. She bowed down with her face to the ground in deference to him and said, “Please help me,[NOTE:2] O king!”
notes: The translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss in reading וַתַּבֹא (vattavoʾ, “and she went”) rather than the MT וַתֹּאמֶר (vattoʾmer, “and she said”). The MT reading shows confusion with וַתֹּאמֶר later in the verse. The emendation suggested here is supported by the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, some mss of the Targum, and Vulgate.
The word “me” is left to be inferred in the Hebrew text; it is present in the Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate.
verses.commentary:
14:4 "spoke to the king" Many later Hebrew MSS, the Targums, the LXX, Peshitta, as well as the Vulgate, have
"came to the king."

▣ "Help, O King" Israeli citizens had the right to ask the king for justice/deliverance/help (cf. 2 Kgs. 6:26).
He was YHWH's judicial representative.

verses.zh: 王问她说：「你有甚么事呢？」回答说：「婢女实在是寡妇，我丈夫死了。
verses.en: The king replied to her, “What do you want?”[NOTE:1] She answered, “I am a widow; my husband is dead.
notes: Heb “What to you?”

verses.zh: 我有两个儿子，一日在田间争斗，没有人解劝，这个就打死那个。
verses.en: Your servant[NOTE:1] has two sons. When the two of them got into a fight in the field, there was no one present who could intervene. One of them struck the other and killed him.
notes: Here and elsewhere (vv. 7, 12, 15a, 17, 19) the woman uses a term which suggests a lower level female servant. She uses the term to express her humility before the king. However, she uses a different term in vv. 15b-16. See the note at v. 15 for a discussion of the rhetorical purpose of this switch in terminology.

verses.zh: 现在全家的人都起来攻击婢女，说：『你将那打死兄弟的交出来，我们好治死他，偿他打死兄弟的命，灭绝那承受家业的。』这样，他们要将我剩下的炭火灭尽，不与我丈夫留名留后在世上。」
verses.en: Now the entire family has risen up against your servant, saying, ‘Turn over the one who struck down his brother, so that we can execute him and avenge the death[NOTE:1] of his brother whom he killed. In so doing we will also destroy the heir.’ They want to extinguish my remaining coal,[NOTE:2] leaving no one on the face of the earth to carry on the name of my husband.”
notes: Heb “in exchange for the life.” The Hebrew preposition ב (bet, “in”) here is the so-called bet pretii, or bet (ב) of price, defining the value attached to someone or something.
My remaining coal is here metaphorical language, describing the one remaining son as her only source of lingering hope for continuing the family line.
verses.commentary:
14:7 "they will extinguish my coal which is left" This imagery has to do with how the people of this period
started their home fires in the morning. Usually a coal or ember from the last night's fire was used. If her last
remaining son is killed, she would have no hope, no remnant, no remembrance of her family's name.

verses.zh: 王对妇人说：「你回家去吧！我必为你下令。」
verses.en: Then the king told the woman, “Go to your home. I will give instructions concerning your situation.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “concerning you.”

verses.zh: 提哥亚妇人又对王说：「我主我王，愿这罪归我和我父家，与王和王的位无干。」
verses.en: The Tekoan woman said to the king, “My lord the king, let any blame fall on me and on the house of my father. But let the king and his throne be innocent!”

verses.zh: 王说：「凡难为你的，你就带他到我这里来，他必不再搅扰你。」
verses.en: The king said, “Bring to me whoever speaks to you, and he won’t bother you again!”

verses.zh: 妇人说：「愿王记念耶和华―你的　神，不许报血仇的人施行灭绝，恐怕他们灭绝我的儿子。」王说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓：你的儿子连一根头发也不致落在地上。」
verses.en: She replied, “In that case,[NOTE:1] let the king invoke the name of[NOTE:2] the Lord your God so that the avenger of blood may not add to the killing! Then they will not destroy my son!” He replied, “As surely as the Lord lives, not a single hair of your son’s head[NOTE:3] will fall to the ground.”
notes: The words “in that case” are not in the Hebrew text, but may be inferred from the context. They are supplied in the translation for the sake of clarification.
Heb “let the king remember.”
Heb “of your son.”
verses.commentary:
14:11 "the Lord your God" This is the covenant name for Israel's Deity
(i.e., YHWH) combined with a general name for deity in the ANE (i.e., Eloah).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

▣ "the avenger of blood" This denotes a member of the family who helps (see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 791, c).
It could be

- the kinsman redeemer (cf. Lev. 25:25,47-55; Ruth 2:20; 4:4,6)

- the blood avenger (cf. Num. 35:19,21; Deut. 19:4-10; Josh. 20:3-5)

In this parable of a brother killing a brother it is uncertain who the blood avenger would be except the
extended family.

The concept of a blood avenger was an OT way of limiting revenge. It was an aspect of the "eye for eye"
legal system of Israel.

▣ "As the Lord lives" This was an oath formula based on a word play between

- the VERB "to be" (BDB 224)

- the covenant name for Israel's God, YHWH (BDB 217)

▣ "not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground" This was an idiom for safety and no retaliation
(cf. 1 Sam. 14:45; 1 Kgs. 1:52).

It may be the source of Jesus saying, "The very hairs of your head are numbered" (Matt. 10:30; Luke 21:18).

verses.zh: 妇人说：「求我主我王容婢女再说一句话。」王说：「你说吧！」
verses.en: Then the woman said, “Please permit your servant to speak to my lord the king about another matter.” He replied, “Tell me.”

verses.zh: 妇人说：「王为何也起意要害　神的民呢？王不使那逃亡的人回来，王的这话就是自证己错了！
verses.en: The woman said, “Why have you devised something like this against God’s people? When the king speaks in this fashion, he makes himself guilty, for the king has not brought back the one he has banished.
verses.commentary:
14:13 As Nathan brought a realization of David's sin, this parable again condemns David for his actions
(i.e., not allowing the heir apparent to return to the capital).

verses.zh: 我们都是必死的，如同水泼在地上，不能收回。　神并不夺取人的性命，乃设法使逃亡的人不致成为赶出、回不来的。
verses.en: Certainly we must die, and are like water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up again. But God does not take away life; instead he devises ways for the banished to be restored.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he devises plans for the one banished from him not to be banished.”
verses.commentary:
14:14 "we will surely die" This is an emphatic Hebrew grammatical structure which involves an
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root
(BDB 559, KB 562).

▣ "Yet God does not take away life, but plans ways so that the banished one will not be cast out from Him"
This statement expresses the basic orientation of YHWH, which is grace, mercy, and forgiveness. Oh my, what a great truth!

The JPSOA interprets this as a reference to King David, not YHWH. "The apparent sense is: God will not
punish you for bringing back the banished Absalom," p. 643.

The MT has a COGNATE ACCUSATIVE, "not to banish" (BDB 623, KB 673, Qal
IMPERFECT) his banished one (same root, Niphal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 我来将这话告诉我主我王，是因百姓使我惧怕。婢女想，不如将这话告诉王，或者王成就婢女所求的。
verses.en: I have now come to speak with my lord the king about this matter, because the people have made me fearful.[NOTE:1] But your servant said, ‘I will speak to the king! Perhaps the king will do what his female servant[NOTE:2] asks.
notes: The LXX (ὄψεταί με, opsetai me) has misunderstood the Hebrew יֵרְאֻנִי (yereʾuni, Piel perfect, “they have made me fearful”), taking the verb to be a form of the verb רָאָה (raʾah, “to see”) rather than the verb יָרֵא (yareʾ, “to fear”). The fact that the Greek translators were working with an unvocalized Hebrew text (i.e., consonants only) made them very susceptible to this type of error.

Here and in v. 16 the woman refers to herself as the king’s אָמָה (ʾamah), a term that refers to a higher level female servant toward whom the master might have some obligation. Like the other term, this word expresses her humility, but it also suggests that the king might have some obligation to treat her in accordance with the principles of justice.
verses.commentary:
14:15 "the people" This could refer to

- the woman's clan or extended family who wanted to kill her only son (2 Sam. 14:7,11,16)

- the people of Israel wanting their handsome heir apparent to return to Jerusalem (v. 13 and possibly v. 17)

verses.zh: 人要将我和我儿子从　神的地业上一同除灭，王必应允救我脱离他的手。
verses.en: Yes![NOTE:1] The king may[NOTE:2] listen and deliver his female servant[NOTE:3] from the hand of the man who seeks to remove[NOTE:4] both me and my son from the inheritance God has given us!’[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “for.”
Or “will.” The imperfect verbal form can have either an indicative or modal nuance. The use of “perhaps” in v. 15b suggests the latter here.
Heb “in order to deliver his maid.”
Heb “destroy.”
Heb “from the inheritance of God.” The expression refers to the property that was granted to her family line in the division of the land authorized by God.
verses.commentary:
14:16 "the hand of the man" This is literally "palm" (BDB 496).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "the inheritance of God" Israel was the inheritance of YHWH. He gave them the land of Canaan
(cf. 1 Sam. 26:19; Ps. 79:1; 136:21; Jer. 2:7). This is imagery from YHWH as "Father."

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

4:17

NASB, NKJV
"be comforting"

NRSV
"will set me at rest"

TEV
"make me safe"

NJB
"restore the peace"

REB
"be a comfort to me"

JPSOA
"provide comfort"

LXX, Peshitta
"be as an offering"

The MT has the FEMININE NOUN (BDB 629) "rest." BDB says "it is a figure for
security and assurance (taken from resting equilibrium of a scale.)"

This word is used of Ruth finding rest (i.e., protection and provision) by marriage (cf. Ruth 1:9).

▣ "for as the angel of God" Does this phrase refer to

- the rest brought by the presence of the Angel of God

- the angel knowing "good and evil" (cf. v. 20; 19:27; NKJV, TEV, NJB)

- David's majesty like the Angel of God (REB)?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE Lord

verses.zh: 婢女又想，我主我王的话必安慰我；因为我主我王能辨别是非，如同　神的使者一样。惟愿耶和华―你的　神与你同在！」
verses.en: So your servant said, ‘May the word of my lord the king be my security, for my lord the king is like the angel of God when it comes to deciding between right and wrong! May the Lord your God be with you!’”

verses.zh: 王对妇人说：「我要问你一句话，你一点不要瞒我。」妇人说：「愿我主我王说。」
verses.en: Then the king replied to the woman, “Don’t hide any information from me when I question you.” The woman said, “Let my lord the king speak.”

verses.zh: 王说：「你这些话莫非是约押的主意吗？」妇人说：「我敢在我主我王面前起誓：王的话正对，不偏左右，是王的仆人约押吩咐我的，这些话是他教导我的。
verses.en: The king said, “Did Joab put you up to all of this?”[NOTE:1] The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, there is no deviation to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king has said. For your servant Joab gave me instructions. He has put all these words in your servant’s mouth.
notes: Heb “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?”
verses.commentary:
14:19 "As your soul lives" This was an oath by the life of the king (cf. 1 Sam. 17:55).

▣ "no one can turn to the right or to the left" This imagery comes from YHWH's truth/covenant as a
"road," "way," or "path." To deviate from the clearly shown way is rebellion. Here, it means no one can lie to the king
who has the discernment of the Angel of God (cf. 2 Sam. 14:20).

verses.zh: 王的仆人约押如此行，为要挽回这事。我主的智慧却如　神使者的智慧，能知世上一切事。」
verses.en: Your servant Joab did this so as to change this situation. But my lord has wisdom like that of the angel of God, and knows everything that is happening in the land.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to know all that is in the land.”
verses.commentary:
14:20 This is obviously hyperbolic language. One reason westerners misinterpret the Bible is that they do not
understand eastern imagery. Two books that have helped me in this area are

- G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible

- D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic

▣ "earth" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH (OT).

verses.zh: 王对约押说：「我应允你这事。你可以去，把那少年人押沙龙带回来。」
verses.en: Then the king said to Joab, “All right! I[NOTE:1] will do this thing. Go and bring back the young man Absalom!”
notes: Many medieval Hebrew mss have “you” rather than “I.”

verses.zh: 约押就面伏于地叩拜，祝谢于王，又说：「王既应允仆人所求的，仆人今日知道在我主我王眼前蒙恩了。」
verses.en: Then Joab bowed down with his face toward the ground and thanked[NOTE:1] the king. Joab said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, because the king has granted the request of your[NOTE:2] servant!”
notes: Heb “blessed.”
The present translation reads with the Qere “your” rather than the MT “his.”

verses.zh: 于是约押起身往基述去，将押沙龙带回耶路撒冷。
verses.en: So Joab got up and went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 王说：「使他回自己家里去，不要见我的面。」押沙龙就回自己家里去，没有见王的面。
verses.en: But the king said, “Let him go over[NOTE:1] to his own house. He may not see my face.” So Absalom went over[NOTE:2] to his own house; he did not see the king’s face.
notes: Heb “turn aside.”
Heb “turned aside.”
verses.commentary:
14:24 Absalom returned from exile but was not fully restored to fellowship with David. Absalom now is the heir
apparent to the throne of Israel. Maybe this is why Joab acted on his behalf.

verses.zh: 以色列全地之中，无人像押沙龙那样俊美，得人的称赞，从脚底到头顶毫无瑕疵。
verses.en: Now in all Israel everyone acknowledged that there was no man as handsome as Absalom.[NOTE:1] From the soles of his feet to the top of his head he was perfect in appearance.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Like Absalom there was not a handsome man in all Israel to boast exceedingly.”
Heb “there was not in him a blemish.”
verses.commentary: 14:25-26 These verses express the cultural expectations of the physical appearance of a king.

verses.zh: 他的头发甚重，每到年底剪发一次；所剪下来的，按王的平称一称，重二百舍客勒。
verses.en: When he would shave his head—at the end of every year he used to shave his head, for it grew too long[NOTE:1] and he would shave it—he used to weigh the hair of his head at three pounds[NOTE:2] according to the king’s weight.
notes: Heb “for it was heavy upon him.”
Heb “two hundred shekels.” The modern equivalent would be about three pounds (1.4 kg).
verses.commentary:
14:26 "shekels" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES.

verses.zh: 押沙龙生了三个儿子，一个女儿。女儿名叫她玛，是个容貌俊美的女子。
verses.en: Absalom had[NOTE:1] three sons and one daughter, whose name was Tamar. She was a very attractive woman.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and there were born.”
The LXX adds here the following words: “And she became a wife to Rehoboam the son of Solomon and bore to him Abia.”
verses.commentary:
14:27 "Tamar" This was Absalom's sister (cf. 2 Sam. 13:1), but now she lived in his house as a daughter
(one protected).

The LXX adds "Tamar. . .and she became wife to Rehoboam son of Solomon and she bore him Abia."
For a possible explanation of this see Hard Sayings of the Bible, p. 245.

2 Samuel 14:27 mentioning three sons is surprising in light of 2 Sam. 18:18. Possibly the sons had died
by chapter 18.

verses.zh: 押沙龙住在耶路撒冷足有二年，没有见王的面。
verses.en: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing the king’s face.
verses.commentary:
14:28-33 This account clearly shows

- the personality of Absalom (v. 30)

- the reluctance of Joab to do more for Absalom (v. 29)

- Absalom's sense that he had not done wrong in killing Amnon (v. 32)

- David's restoration of Absalom would prove to be a problem (2 Samuel 15-18)

verses.zh: 押沙龙打发人去叫约押来，要托他去见王，约押却不肯来。第二次打发人去叫他，他仍不肯来。
verses.en: Then Absalom sent a message to Joab asking him to send him to the king, but Joab[NOTE:1] was not willing to come to him. So he sent a second message to him, but he still was not willing to come.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 所以押沙龙对仆人说：「你们看，约押有一块田，与我的田相近，其中有大麦，你们去放火烧了。」押沙龙的仆人就去放火烧了那田。
verses.en: So he said to his servants, “Look, Joab has a portion of field adjacent to mine and he has some barley there. Go and set it on fire.”[NOTE:1] So Absalom’s servants set Joab’s[NOTE:2] portion of the field on fire.
notes: The LXX adds here the following words: “And the servants of Absalom burned them up. And the servants of Joab came to him, rending their garments. They said….”
The word “Joab’s” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
14:30 "set it on fire" The MT has the VERB, BDB 428, KB 429, Hiphil
PERFECT with waw. But the Masoretic scholars suggested it be understood as a Hiphil
IMPERATIVE to match, "go" (Qal IMPERATIVE).

verses.zh: 于是约押起来，到了押沙龙家里，问他说：「你的仆人为何放火烧了我的田呢？」
verses.en: Then Joab got up and came to Absalom’s house. He said to him, “Why did your servants set my portion of field on fire?”

verses.zh: 押沙龙回答约押说：「我打发人去请你来，好托你去见王，替我说：『我为何从基述回来呢？不如仍在那里。』现在要许我见王的面；我若有罪，任凭王杀我就是了。」
verses.en: Absalom said to Joab, “Look, I sent a message to you saying, ‘Come here so that I can send you to the king with this message:[NOTE:1] “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.”’ Let me now see the face of the king. If I am at fault, let him put me to death!”
notes: Heb “saying.”

verses.zh: 于是约押去见王，将这话奏告王，王便叫押沙龙来。押沙龙来见王，在王面前俯伏于地，王就与押沙龙亲嘴。
verses.en: So Joab went to the king and informed him. The king[NOTE:1] summoned Absalom, and he came to the king. Absalom[NOTE:2] bowed down before the king with his face toward the ground and the king kissed him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he.” Joab, acting on behalf of the king, may be the implied subject.
Heb “he”; the referent (Absalom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Absalom.” For stylistic reasons the name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation.
verses.commentary:
14:33 "the king kissed Absalom" This was a gesture of full restoration, acceptance, or feeling of love
(cf. Gen. 33:4; 45:15; Exod. 18:7; Ruth 1:9,14; 1 Sam. 10:1; 20:41).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is an avenger of blood?

- Why was the restoration of Absalom important for Israel?

- In what sense is David like the Angel of God?

- Is the Tamar in 2 Sam. 14:22 a daughter of Absalom or a way to refer to his sister?

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
